A couple of months back I started to collate some data to determine
which clans and bloodlines haven't really been presented in the CCG yet.
Much of the info obtained are from various web sources, as I don't own
many of the RPG books *sniff*

Figured to go ahead and share what I have, as it only does so much good
on my hard drive. Per my recollection, there are maybe a few groups
I may have missed, but figured that the following were the most feasable
to see print in a set.

It should go to show that there is substantial uncovered territory
remaining for White Wolf to explore, which should keep us all happy for
some time to come.

Bernie

======================================================
Remaining Vampire clans/concepts for exploration:

Black Hand
The Black Hand is a sect within a sect, an elite group of vampires
recognized as separate from all other Sabbat. The Black Hand (or simply
the Hand) is not truly a separate body. However, since all its members
are loyal to the Sabbat over all else.

The Black Hand is composed primarily of Assamite Antitribu, as well as
many of the more militant vampires from other clans. The members of the
Hand do not exist in packs of their own. Rather, they are members of
normal Sabbat packs. while most Black Hand vampires are tough, their
irate packmates quickly put them in their place if they overstep
themselves

Assamite Antitribu
Description: The shock troops of the Sabbat's Black Hand. Much like
their brethren with one exception - they never accepted the Tremere's
curse.
Disciplines: Celerity, Obfuscate, Quietus
Weaknesses: Easily addicted to Kindred Vitae. Any time an Assamite
Antitribu tastes blood outside the Vaulderie, must make an Instincts
roll at Blood Points drunk+3. If fails, Kindred frenzies, and attempts
to drink as much blood as possible.

Ravnos Antitribu
Description: Much like the Nos, it is hard to tell Clan and antitribu
apart.
Disciplines: Animalism, Chimerstry, Fortitude
Weaknesses: Must make a self-control roll to prevent self from
committing her crime of choice when the opportunity presents itself

Children of Osiris
Somehow made once more into mortals by Osiris
Description: The light in the shadows. Hunters of their own kind, and
blood enemies of the Setites.
Disciplines: [Chose three] Bardo, Obeah, Thaumaturgy, Serpentis,
Dominate, Protean
Weakness: Weak Blood

Laibon (bloodline)
Description: Strange guardians of the tribes of Africa. Filled with
wanderlust they act as dark protectors and medicine men.
Disciplines: Abombwe, Animalism, Fortitude
Weaknesses: If a Laibon expends or ingests Blood Points, the Beast
automatically consumes a point.

Nictuku (Sabbat)
Disciplines: Obfuscate, Quietus, Grotequous
Weaknesses: Like the Nosferatu, the Nictuku have an appearance of 0 and
automatically fail any rolls having to do with appearance. Actually,
thanks to their horrible aura, they can barely interact with humans at
all.
Description: It is said that the Nictuku are the true clan, and that the
Nosferatu are a bloodline of the Nictuku. Fortunately for the person who
said this, he didn't say it around a Nosferatu.

Kindred of the East (Bushi / Gaki)
Disciplines: (Bushi) - Celerity, Kai, Presence (Gaki) - Auspex,
Dominate, Rift
Weaknesses:
Description: Kindred of the East are the eastern vampires, who are not
really Kindred at all, but a completely different kind of vampire, who
call themselves Kuei-Jin. The Kuei-Jin have all died and returned from a
hell they call the Yomi Worlds to their own bodies. While they can feed
on blood they take life-force (Chi) in general. Their powers are not
dependant upon blood but age and enlightenment. The Kuei-Jin and the
Kindred have a rather poor relationship.

It is no mere coincidence that the Gaki are known as hungry ghosts. All
Gaki must expend two blood points per day, instead of the usual one
required of Western Kindred. Additionally, the difficulties in resisting
Hunger Frenzy are two levels higher, much like the Brujah. Gaki means
the hungry dead in Japanese.

Seraphim (Bloodline)
Description: Demon or angel? Who knows? Least of all them.
Disciplines: Daimoinon, Vicissitude, Visceratika
Weaknesses: Their natural appearance of Zero is distinctive, but can and
is changed at will. They have amnesia concerning their mortal memories.
As they are descended from Gargoyles, they are at -1 Willpower to resist
any form of mind control. And their particular weakness is that only a
single Seraph from each generation can produce progeny. Those
individuals are named the Archangels, and all the rest have the flaw:
Infertile Vitae.
http://www.patman.org/wod/alternate/altclans/seraphim.asp

Serpents of the Light (Bloodline)
Description: Sabbat Setites
Disciplines: Obfuscate, Presence, Serpentis
Weaknesses: Extremely susceptible to sunlight (double damage.) Subtract
one from all dice pools while in bright light (spotlights, strobes,
etc.)

Old Clan Tzimisce
Description: Lodged in the heart of the Carpathians, they still survive,
nursing the wounds of the Anarch Wars
Various Houses of Tzimisce possess differing discipline spreads

Tlacique: Warriors of Set
Obfuscate, Presence, Protean ?? or is it
Potence, Presence, Serpentis
Potence, Presence, Protean **
The "default" predatory form for Shape of the Beast is a jaguar, rather
than a wolf

Inconnu?

Bahari (aka: Followers of Lilith)
Disciplines: Obsfucate, Potence, Sublimate

> > Black Hand

This is only a very recent development in light of the Final Nights. IIRC
the accord struck between the Hand and the Sabbat heirarchy after the last
Sabbat Civil War actually required the Hand the distribute it's members
amongst normal packs for mutual peace of mind.

One thing you haven't mentioned is the distinction between the Lost Tribe
and the Tal'Mahe'Ra. Both were Gehenna cults of sorts, and ended up merging
to become the Black Hand as they are in modern times. The latter were much
more secretive though, and many Hand members were not aware that a 'double
membership' was going on around them involving this Tal'Mahe'Ra or 'True
Hand' as well. The True Hand were like a sect within a sect, but their plans
were scuppered when their secret headquarters in the Shadowlands (the
shadow-city of Enoch) was bombed to Oblivion by the Smiling Lord of the
Heirarchy (see the Wraith: the Oblivion RPG for more info).

(As an aside, this same event explains why the Giovanni have lost contact
with many of their wraith contacts, and why their remaining ghostly servants
are so hard to retain and control. This event also explains the sudden
appearance of demons in the world, as depicted by the Demon: The Fallen RPG)

> Packs don't really have much of a theme in V:tES though. Maybe a concept
> that could be tweaked in somehow? (hint hint).

It's difficult to see how packs could become significant in regards to the
overall metagame. It may be worth lobbying for more action and reaction
cards that involve 'other' or 'multiple' vampires (similar to Sanguinus) but
which are sect-based instead of Discipline-based. I guess we'll have to wait
and see eh? :)

"Curse?" <snaps fingers> "What Curse?"

IMHO Ur-Shulgi is probably the most powerful vampire awake as depicted in
the Vampire RPG and the associated fiction. He demanded that all of Haqim's
bloodline return to the Mountain for a test of loyalty. Those that served
any master or god other than Haqim himself were destroyed, with only the
most loyal being permitted to remain alive.

Hence why the majority of the viziers and magicians of the clan legged it
when they had the chance, together with those who never returned to the
mountain to be tested, they now make up the new 'antitribu' and as a group
are petitioning to join the Camarilla (as much for protection as much as
anything else).

small, exclusive Gehenna Cult rather than a bloodline.

have surivived to the modern day. However, given many deceased Dark Ages
characters have been brought to life anyway in the CCG, anything's possible!

lady

There are many names given for them in various sourcebooks, but in fact it's
actually all conjecture. They've never been properly documented or explained
(IMHO a good thing) but they're great for keeping your PCs in suspense... :)

Well IIRC the names still mean something, but they have been reinterpreted
through the Kindred of the East material. The original Disciplines have been
entirely replaced though.

> > Seraphim (Bloodline)

> > Inconnu?
>

> officially written about these guys for a very long time to the best of my
> knowledge. And a lot of what was writtem is not canon. This is probably
> because a lot of what was written was utter shite.

Yup again I'm glad WW have kept these guys largely a mystery. The sect
definitely exists, and Inconnu Monitors are included in several city
sourcebooks for Vampire. The story goes that after the fall of Rome, and
then Consantinople, a number of elders grew disgusted at the consequences of
their political maneuvering and withdrew from all Kindred affairs entirely.
They are allegedly mostly Ventrue, Malkavian and True Brujah and although
they try to keep tabs on what is happening, they never get involved or lend
their support.

TBH all the official modern-day bloodlines were included in the Bloodlines
card set that we've seen already. The only additional factions from the
canon RPG that might be worth a mention are:

- 'Old clan' Tzimisce, sometimes collectively referred to as the Oradea
League, who had Dominate instead of Vicissitude as a clan Discipline. These
guys survived the Anarch Revolt and the formation of the Sabbat and would
definitely be Scarce in the CCG. They've hardly been mentioned in the
Revised edition game though, and Achilli may have binned them altogether
without us knowing.

- Surviving Cappadocians. Lazarus the progeny of Cappadocius is rumoured to
still be alive, and if so he may have sired more of his own. In the CCG they
would probably get their own Discipline to contrast them from the Giovanni
and the Samedi. Again these guys would definitely be Scarce.

- The bloodline of aquatic vampires who mainly live in the sea referred to
by Blood-Dimmed Tides (a Werewolf sourcebook). Bit stupid if you ask me, but
could be fun I guess... :)

- The Sabbat Inquisition, another mini-sect within the Sabbat devoted to
rooting out and eradicating infernalism

- The many various Gehenna Cults within the Camarilla

The new sourcebook for Africa has just come out for the RPG though, and
there might be new stuff in there that we could add to the list. And that's
not even starting all the other types of mortal and supernatural creatures
that could be included as allies, retainers, or even as new types of minion
cards...

Regards,

Mike

Maybe so, but there were some problems with distribution of power in the
Bloodlines release. Best guess is when you only have so many card slots
to work with you do the best that you can. Besides, you always what to
leave your audience "wanting more".

Bloodlines has partial success. It would be really nice to have a
complimentary expansion to shore up the weak points.

From my article "A Look at Bloodlines"
==================================
A look at Bloodlines:

Bloodlines was released for the experienced deckbuilder with
the premise that the new minor clans would inject some new life
into the game. Ambitious in scope, achieved partial success in
execution. Let's face it, Bloodlines is an incomplete experience.

We play card games primarily for 3 reasons
1. They provide entertainment
2. A good CCG maintains a level competetive environment
3. The chance to build more social ties

In regards to Bloodlines, it succeeds on points 1&3 while failing
point 2. By design, Bloodlines was developed to mix in with existing
cards to create new strategies. Unfortunately, almost the entire set
needs a shot in the arm so as to compete on a level playing field.

V:TES design takes it's cues from the World of Darkness such that the
designers didn't want to give these minor clans too much power.
If too effective, they could dethrone the primary clans from their
dominance in the CCG (Ventrue, Pander, Ravnos, etc.).
So what we have now are a number of minor clans that see marginal
play, as thier potential to win is hampered by lack of resources.

If the bloodlines were without any real power, they would have
been wiped out long ago.
==================================

I could probably elaborate on a few of the points above if necessary.

Let's just say that while I did like Bloodlines, it came across as an
incomplete experience. That's not what a good CCG expansion should
strive for.

Messages.Author: The Fanboy
Messages.Body:
> If the bloodlines were without any real power, they would have
> been wiped out long ago.

Ah, but looking at the V:TM storyline, they do with great frequency
die out.

The Salubri were once a clan. They lost that status when Tremere
diablerized Saulot. Then, they were rapidly slaughtered by the
Tremere and their allies, to such an extent that up until recently
only 7 remained. One decided to eschew the survivor's agenda of
suriviving through flying under radar, and embraced the swarm tactics
of the Sabbat - resulting in the Antitribu.

The Salubri survive BECAUSE they have no real power. Because of this,
they routinely escape notice. The Antitribu are a very (past five
years) new development.

The Gargoyles exist because it is convenient for the Tremere that they
exist. They are creations of the Tremere, who have the power to keep
them alive.

The Blood Brothers exist because it was convenient to the Sabbat that
they exist. With the loss of the Tremere Antitribu, the sect has lost
it's ability to create more Blood Brothers. Within a decade, they'll
likely be gone.

The Harbingers have just emerged from a stasis imposed by their
founder, who was diablerized by Giovanni centuries ago. They, too,
are a recent phenomenon (past five years). Had they not been put in
stasis, they would have been killed with the rest of their brethren.

The Daughters are only a few centuries old (1700's at the oldest), and
have no real power to themselves. Most exist because they're mistaken
as Toreador, and as long as they keep making pretty music, the
Toreador don't care.

The Samedi aren't much older, and surivive because their mistaken as
Nosferatu, and as long as they avoid the sewers, the Nosferatu really
don't care.

The Ahrimanes are already dead. They died in the last five years.

The True Brujah and Nagarajah are fading fast. Their numbers, always
low, have dwindled rapidly since the Week of Nightmares.

The Baali survived extinction at the hands of the Salubri because they
got the Tremere to kill the Salubri. They're frequently mistaken as
Setites. Even by Setites.

The Kiasyd are a creation of the Sabbat, and exist so long as they
serve the sect's purposes.

White Wolf Canon is loaded with bloolines that haven't survived -- the
Lamia and the Lhiannon are two of my favorites, but there are more.
That's the tragedy of the bloodlines -- they're constantly in danger
of dying out.

Fanboy

Blood Brothers may not have that much flexibility, but the 7 Sanguinus
cards are almost exactly right for the clan:

Octopod is supdily good compared to Blur
Coag Enitity is the rush you HAVE to block
Gestalt is an awesome blocking card
Walk of Cain gives a bleed boost not reachable by most bruise decks
Brothers Blood gives great resource management potential
Unnatural Bond is a great gen option
Coordianted attacks is a bit average

So only one of the 7 cards is mediocre, leaving 6 very strong cards
that work with extreme focus for the intended focus of the clan. Sure,
the BBs are a one trick pony, but they are almost uniquely set up
above all over clans in the game to do that trick.

All the new disciplines need a boost. Sure,
> you might squeeze some Daughters in with the Ventrue,

The Daughters are strong even on their own as power voters with more
stealth than their ventrue or toreador "cousins". Melpomine beats the
crap out of Presence in politics, and they have Presence for bleeds.
Plus they are all pretty cheap making for an efficient crypt design.

Don't forget the new tech that was introduced - Choir. Although a way
off perfect, this is pretty close to a new way of ousting -
unbounceable "bleeds" which are stackable more so than Enticement.
Tricky, but do-able.

With little effort you can get a competitive set of vampires going
outside of the initial 5.

compliements Animalism extrmemly well. I have yet to see the Ahrimanes
used to even half their potential after a year. They are possibly the
strongest unit to come out of Bloodlines.

> And I'm certain a bunch of people can post a bunch of "tournament
> winning" decks built around Bloodlines. But why only do the job half
> assed? What is stopping WW doing a Bloodlines boost expansion?

They may well do so in time, but considering the impact that only a
fraction of the set has had on the game, you've got to give it a bit
of time to figure out where to take it:

My arguement as to why Bloodlines is the best thing we have seen since
the original VTES set:

It was the most igeniously thought out set since the original set. It
came close to changing the way we approached decks with the quality of
the cards and the ingenuity of execution. It introduced the "double
discipline" card (more poke for your money, less general utility due
to the need for 2 disciplines). It introduced the multi discipline
card - mainly as a reaction to the short order of discipline users,
but still gave excellent utility. Introducing "Scare", "Infernal", and
"Sterile" disadvantages all gave us something to think about, and
these are all totally fair for the power you get.

You want examples of why the set was good?

1) Mattieus. Every (and I mean EVERY) tournament I have seen in the
last year has had a deck that features this tank of a vampire. In the
last 2 tournies I've been at, his presence on the table meant that one
deck was totally screwed - since his "other" special screws Setite
casual bleeds. I saw a Night moves / enticement deck using setites die
as it couldn't get the edge at all. Stupidly good, but without
overdoing it.

2) Lee Dinh Zho. Another perennial favourite. His ability is, again, a
hot tip and he shows up like a bad smell to most events.

3) Call the Great Beast. It was great to see Jon Cooper win a
tournament with a deck centred around this, but the imagination that
went into this card was superb.

4) Nose of the Hound. This card shows up more than Ambush in most
decks I've seen lately. It's amazing how many combat monsters have
Aus!

This is of the top of my head. There are many, many more examples of
individual cards that have real power and have changed what people
bring to events.

The cards have had a massive impact on the scene and a huge number of
decks utiliise Bloodlines cards... arguably more so that CE. The cards
are competitive and imaginiative.

Compare to Final Nights (mainly the vampires are used). Most of the
"new" cards in that set rarely see the light of day (Banner of
Nutrality? Thrones Crumble? Venitian Conference?) simply becuase
there are better ways of doing things by the clans in question.
However, with Bloodlines, since options are pretty limited, we see the
majority of the availible cards used when someone elects to play. As
such, there isn't much of the set that has not been seen at a
tournament in the last year.

The only two downsides, as pointed out above, come in the form of 2
clans who were below par. However, compare to the Nosferatu (around
nearly 10 years and still pretty weak on the whole) and the caitiff /
pander (now "bargain basement crypt-fillers" at best) the Samedi and
the !Salubri are reasonably competant.

Bloodlines is fine as it is, but as has been mentioned is NOT for the
casual player, it's designed for the player that has a deep
understanding of the game and wants to try something different.

DH

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In message <3ec4c620...@netnews.attbi.com>,

berni...@attbi.comHOLDLeSPAM writes:
>>Thus the Bloodlines clans are good, though they are not in the top tier (but as
>>James mentioned, they're not *supposed* to be).
>
>Which is flawed thinking (by the designers, not James) when you're
>trying to sell an expansion of cards to players that want to build decks
>around wacky clans, rather then use the whole set as filler for other
>stuff.

Possibly.

There are two obvious ways of doing "wacky cards". One is Magic:
Unglued - make them entirely fun and optional. Then you can do
different things which will never impact on the game as a whole.

Let us assume that we don't choose that route, however. We choose a
route where they'll be real cards in the real game.

Now, do we make everything super-wacky? And each clan can do its own
wacky thing in its own wacky way and win? Well, we could. But doesn't
that turn into Rage? Effectively, here's a new expansion that
completely changes the whole face of the game - not just by adding new
cards, but by completely changing the face of what is done and how it's
done.[0]

One obvious integration method is to use them as real clans. Just make
them absolutely normal. They interact with the game in the same old
way. They're called the Salubri, but you've got 15 of them, and they
could just as easily be Ravnos or Brujah. And you make their cards
exactly the same power level as the rest of the game.

One other obvious integration method is to make them limited in some
fashion, but with unique facets. They become interesting, but
vulnerable, stepping outside some of the obvious tenets of the *rest* of
the game, but doing so in a fashion that is inherently screwed over by
some other issues.

>If you could buy a Pound of Steak or a Pound of Meatloaf at the same
>price, which would you be likely to spend your money on? (Sorry, we
>don't serve Veggies in the WoD).

Taking a food metaphor, then.

You start off with a meal. It's very basic, but everything works.
Roast lamb, some mashed potato, some peas... everything pretty much
works together, though there's some variety. You want to extend the
meal. So you pick interesting things that provide flavour and texture,
but that otherwise blend in seamlessly. The Ravnos are the gravy, the
Lasombra are the parsnips.

Now we want to add wacky clans. Pour some custard on top. Throw a few
cherries in. And wrap the edge of the plate in squirty cream.

Or perhaps you add a little on the side. It changes the flavour of the
meal overall, but doesn't overall detract from the experience, enhancing
the experience for those that want it without forcing everyone to pay
attention.

One fundamental problem with the line of thought is:

"when you're trying to sell an expansion of cards to players
that want to build decks around wacky clans"

Are you? Are you indeed?

Now, if you can sell a stand-alone set for players that want to build
wacky clans that won't impact on the game for everyone else, they can
have their fun. (In some ways, this is mirrored in the World of
Darkness setting - those wanting power-combat can play Game X, those
wanting deep philosophical torment can play Game Y.)

You have to remember that the way that Bloodlines was implemented means
that it impacts on the game - maybe not as heavily as it could, but it
still impacts. So what you're trying to do is not as simple as "sell an
expansion of cards to players that want..." You're also remembering
that you don't want to scare off all the players who don't want the game
changing beneath their feet.

How many people threw up their hands and said "I'm not going to play"
when things like 7/7 happened? How many more would look at a full-blown
wacky clan Bloodlines and say "This is a completely different game to
the one I signed up for"?

Yet at the same time, Bloodlines as it was implemented allows for a
great deal of subtlety on the part of players. No-one is runaway
unstoppable, and many of the cards can be brought in anyway. For
instance, Strength of the Bear can still be very useful to Animalism
decks. I wouldn't say no to it with a Gangrel deck, for instance.
Extra damage on an aggravated hand strike? I wouldn't say no.

But if you go for super-wacky as opposed to temperate wacky, you either
lose that option (because the clans now stand up for themselves
entirely) or you go unbalanced by leaving it in.

By creating a set of wacky clans that do wacky things in wacky ways, how
many players are you going to scare off?

[0] This is particularly exacerbated in some games by a lack of generic
defence (many actions in V:TES are vulnerable to generic intercept) and
multiple, changing victory conditions - which are added to.
